claims.text: Under conventional casting, Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms multiple primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during solidification.
Electromagnetic levitation provides containerless melting and solidification.
Electromagnetic levitation suppresses heterogeneous nucleation in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Suppressing heterogeneous nucleation will increase amorphous retention in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Electromagnetic levitation will enhance the thermal stability of amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Container walls and impurities provide heterogeneous nucleation sites during conventional processing.
Removing or reducing heterogeneous nucleation sites promotes deeper melt undercooling.
Deeper undercooling reduces the likelihood of primary crystalline phase formation.
Reduced primary crystallization enhances formation and retention of the amorphous phase.
Levitation-processed samples will have a higher amorphous fraction than conventionally container-cast samples cooled under otherwise identical conditions.
Levitation-processed samples will exhibit delayed or reduced crystallization during reheating.
Electromagnetic levitation will shift the crystallization onset temperature relative to conventional casting.
The intervention's benefits require sufficiently high cooling rates.
Reheating should remain below the temperature at which crystallization typically accelerates.
Stable electromagnetic levitation depends on compatible sample size and composition.
The optimal levitation frequency, power, and cooling and reheating windows for amorphous retention are undetermined.

contradictions.description: The reheating protocol is stated to remain below the conventional crystallization onset, but the experiment proposes using DSC to identify and compare crystallization onset temperatures and crystallization exotherms. Measuring those endpoints ordinarily requires heating through the crystallization range, so the stated reheating boundary conflicts with the proposed measurement unless a separate DSC scan is intended.
